question: Who started the first organized nursing school that set the standard for modern training?
explanation: Florence Nightingale opened the first organized nursing training school at St. Thomas' Hospital in London, completely changing how nurses were prepared for practice. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h1)

question: Before formal nursing schools existed, how was care mostly provided to sick people in the early days?
explanation: Before modern training, caring for the sick was mostly handled by religious institutions, monasteries, and family members relying on charity rather than formal medical science. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h1)

question: Who brought the earliest Western-style healthcare and nursing training sites to Nigeria?
explanation: Christian missions played a huge role by setting up the earliest mission hospitals and clinics, which laid the foundation for modern healthcare training in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why did early Nigerian nursing education follow the British system so closely?

options.A: Local laws strictly banned traditional healing practices
options.B: British colonial administration shaped the initial healthcare framework
options.C: There were no local languages suitable for medical instruction
options.D: Nigerian nurses demanded identical uniforms to British nurses

explanation: Since Nigeria was under British colonial rule back then, the healthcare structures and professional rules set up during that era were directly copied from Britain. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which official body is responsible for regulating nursing and midwifery education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the legal authority that sets the rules for nursing education, student registration, and professional practice across Nigeria. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a major benefit of moving nursing education toward university degree programs?

options.A: Shortening the time spent in training by half
options.C: Enhancing critical thinking and research skills
options.D: Eliminating the need for clinical hospital practice

explanation: University degree programs combine deep academic study with research, helping nurses handle complex health situations using evidence-based care. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h3)

question: Nursing informatics is a blend of which three main fields?

options.A: Public health, sociology, and medical anthropology
options.D: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: Nursing informatics combines nursing knowledge with computer and communication tech to help manage patient data smoothly. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h4)

question: How do electronic health records (EHRs) help keep patients safe on the ward?

options.A: By reducing handwriting errors and improving access to accurate medication histories
options.B: By ensuring patients never experience hospital readmissions
options.C: By replacing the need for physical patient assessments entirely
options.D: By cutting down the total number of staff required on duty

explanation: Digital records get rid of messy handwriting and make it easy to share correct drug orders, which massively cuts down on medication mistakes. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h4)

question: Evidence-Based Practice (EBP) asks a nurse to combine which three things?

options.A: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient preferences
options.B: Traditional customs and doctor's personal opinions
options.C: Hospital management policies and insurance guidelines
options.D: Textbook theory from older generations of nurses

explanation: EBP is all about combining solid research, your own clinical judgment as a nurse, and what the patient values to give them the best care possible. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT part of an advanced nurse's clinical role?

options.C: Bridging healthcare gaps in underserved areas

explanation: Advanced nursing is all about direct patient care, specialized health checks, and treatment duties—not balancing the hospital's financial books! [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main reason behind the current 'brain drain' trend among Nigerian nurses?

options.A: Desire to learn completely different traditional healing methods
options.B: Mandatory global exchange programs set by the government
options.C: A complete ban on nursing practice within the country
options.D: Search for better remuneration and improved working conditions abroad

explanation: Many skilled Nigerian nurses move overseas because of better pay, better hospital facilities, and much more supportive work environments. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h6)

question: How do severe staff shortages directly affect nurses working in local Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: They automatically grant nurses higher administrative authority
options.B: They guarantee increased salaries for the remaining workers
options.C: They eliminate the need to document patient care procedures
options.D: They lead to heavy workloads, physical fatigue, and increased stress

explanation: When there are too few nurses to look after a massive crowd of patients, the heavy workload naturally leads to intense physical tiredness and burnout. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h6)
